title: Yoneda extensions and derived Ext in every positive degree
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with derived Ext groups [def-pc-ext], and let $U,V\in\mathcal A$ and $i\geq1$. A degree-$i$ Yoneda extension of $U$ by $V$ is an exact sequence $0\to V\to E_{i-1}\to\cdots\to E_0\to U\to0$. Equivalence is generated by morphisms of such exact sequences that are the identity on $V$ and $U$; the addition is the Baer sum, obtained by direct sum, pullback along the diagonal of $U$, and pushout along addition on $V$. The canonical map sending this sequence to its class $U[0]\to V[0][i]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ induces a natural isomorphism of abelian groups from Yoneda extension classes to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal A}(U,V)$ of [def-pc-ext]. In degree one the zero class consists exactly of split short exact sequences. If $V$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], these groups vanish for every $i>0$.

proof.text: Construct the signed class using actual successive cokernel cuts, and prove the degree-one split-zero criterion by the contravariant Ext exact sequence.
Naturality makes the concrete class invariant under endpoint-fixed arrows; induction on EqvGen makes it invariant under zigzags. Quot.lift gives the map on classes.
Surjectivity and equality detection make the quotient map bijective. Transport the abelian group structure along Equiv.ofBijective, so no arbitrary existence witness is used to define the comparison.
The degree-one normalization is the defining equation. The signed splice identity supplies the splice normalization; naturality is inherited from the concrete class.

For BaerSum data, apply naturality to the two product projections, the diagonal pullback map, and the addition pushout map. Bilinearity and the diagonal-projection identities give delta(G)=delta(E)+delta(F). Injectivity of the quotient comparison proves the Baer field. The geometric construction exists by the separate exact-sequence result.

Use the proved degree-one zero criterion. For injective vanishing, specialize Mathlib CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.subsingleton_of_injective U V n (EnoughInjectives.lean:110); this result itself assumes only that V is injective, not enough injectives.
